rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L08.html section 5 (line 272): containment, monotone expected maximum, and the null-win statement
rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: Re-derived. Let Q_N be the maximum of N null statistics and X_N the new null. Q_N = max(Q_(N-1), X_N) >= Q_(N-1) pointwise, for any joint law of the statistics. (a) E[Q_N] >= E[Q_(N-1)]: the expected maximum cannot fall as N grows. (b) {Z + delta > Q_N} is a subset of {Z + delta > Q_(N-1)}, so the probability that the genuine configuration wins cannot rise (containment, the T span that was already at 584f614). (c) The complement: P(some null beats the genuine) = 1 - P(genuine wins) cannot fall, so 'the null configurations win at least as often' (T). Bound: Lesson 1 Theorem 2.1 (L01.html line 82) states 'Let Z_1, ..., Z_N each have the standard normal distribution, with any joint distribution, and N >= 2. Then E[max Z_n] <= sqrt(2 ln N)'; its proof (Jensen, e^(lambda E M) <= sum E e^(lambda Z_n) = N e^(lambda^2/2), then lambda = sqrt(2 ln N)) is re-derived and holds with no independence. Numerical spot check (scratch scripts/l08_sec5_monotone.py, seed 777, 60,000 draws, N up to 60; output out_l08_sec5_monotone.txt): E[max] of the first N is non-decreasing in N for an equicorrelated law (rho 0.9), independent normals, a comonotone law and a block-random law; at every N it lies below sqrt(2 ln N) (smallest margins 0.9973, 0.5416, 1.1820 and 0.5990); P(genuine wins) with k nulls, k = 1..39, is non-increasing (0.8778, 0.8185, 0.7111, 0.6612, 0.5417, ... ). All checks pass.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/cards.json S7-c158 (L07): grade T, theorem-only back
rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: Re-checked. The back now says only what Proposition 5.4 proves: "It uses V1 + V2 instead of theta. For jointly normal returns with a common per-period Sharpe ratio SR and SR^2 < 2 (Proposition 5.4) it is undersized under positive correlation and oversized under negative correlation. In general it is oversized exactly when theta > V1 + V2." Proposition 5.4 (line 426-428) gives the limit 2(1 - Phi(z sqrt((V1+V2)/theta))), which is below alpha when theta < V1+V2 and above when theta > V1+V2. Re-derived: Corollary 5.2 gives theta = 2(1-rho) + (SR1^2 + SR2^2)/2 - SR1 SR2 rho^2 and V_i = 1 + SR_i^2/2, so for a common SR, theta - (V1+V2) = -rho(2 + SR^2 rho), whose sign is -sign(rho) when SR^2 < 2 (since 2 + SR^2 rho >= 2 - SR^2 > 0). Monte Carlo (4e6 draws, scratch math_checks.py, math_checks_out.txt) confirms the closed form for theta to 0.0035 at the largest deviation across rho in {-0.9,...,0.9} and three SR pairs. No numbers on this card. T is correct. [8352c53: cards.json changed for S7-c154, S7-c161 and S7-c219 and gained S7-c223 (L07) and other units' cards; this card is unchanged (git diff checked).]

rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: Round-10 FAIL re-checked from scratch at 50d202e. (1) Grade: the back states a derived result: with SR_n = 0 and a constant omitted cost k the recorded SR is SR_n + k/sigma_n = delta_n > 0 (recorded mean mu + k, sigma unchanged), the estimate converges in probability to delta_n (limiting SR as the lesson defines it), while the luck hurdle sqrt(2 ln N / T) (L01 formula (2), Corollary 2.2) and the Bonferroni hurdle Phi^-1(1 - alpha/N)/sqrt(T) (L02) both tend to 0 like 1/sqrt(T) at fixed N and alpha; so P(SR-hat > hurdle) -> 1. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/cards.json S7-c212 (L08, new, grade T); course/modules/S/S7/L08.html section 5; key-results row 858
rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: Claim: adding a null trial cannot raise the probability that a genuine configuration wins in sample, whatever the joint law. Proof (re-derived): let X0 be the genuine in-sample statistic and M_k the maximum of k null statistics. The winning event with k nulls is {X0 > M_k}; adding a null Y gives {X0 > max(M_k, Y)}, which is contained in {X0 > M_k}, so its probability cannot exceed the earlier one. No independence or distributional assumption is used. Numerical spot check (scratch scripts/spot_checks.py, 400,000 draws, a common-factor joint law, N-1 = 0,1,4,9,39 nulls): the win probability is non-increasing at every size (for example 0.6448 -> 0.4817 when a second null is added, 0.0513 -> 0.0502 at 39 nulls). The card's back matches Section 5's text. Grade T is right (a proof on the page). PASS. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L07.html Corollary 5.2 (line 405-410), Proposition 5.4 (line 425-431), key-results rows 747-748
rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: New row; re-derived and spot-checked numerically (scratch math_checks.py, output math_checks_out.txt). Influence of the Sharpe estimator for standardized return u: psi = u - (SR/2)(u^2 - 1); Var psi = 1 + SR^2/2; Cov(psi1, psi2) = rho + SR1 SR2 rho^2 / 2 (Isserlis: E[u1 u2] = rho, E[u1 u2^2] = 0, E[u1^2 u2^2] = 1 + 2 rho^2). Hence theta = Var(psi1 - psi2) = 2(1 - rho) + (SR1^2 + SR2^2)/2 - SR1 SR2 rho^2, the Corollary 5.2 formula (row 747). Monte Carlo with 4,000,000 draws for SR pairs (0.05,0.05), (0.1,0.3), (0.5,1.0) and rho in {-0.9,-0.5,0,0.5,0.9}: largest |MC - closed form| = 0.0035, consistent with MC error. Sign check (common SR in {0.05, 0.5, 1.3, 1.41}, rho in +-{0.1, 0.5, 0.99}): sign(theta - (V1+V2)) = -sign(rho) for every point. So Proposition 5.4's "undersized under positive correlation, oversized under negative" holds for SR^2 < 2. The limit (line 427) follows from Theorem 5.1, sqrt((T-1)/T) -> 1 and Slutsky's lemma, as the proof on lines 433-436 states; the proof's identity (V1+V2) - theta = rho(2 + SR^2 rho) (line 436) matches the derivation above. PASS. rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: Re-derived at d10fb51. Monotonicity: with N+1 nulls the maximum is the pointwise maximum over N nulls and one more variable, so it is at least the N-null maximum for every outcome, and its expectation cannot fall. Bound: for any joint law of Z_1..Z_N standard normal, e^{lambda E max Z_n} <= E e^{lambda max Z_n} (Jensen) <= sum_n E e^{lambda Z_n} = N e^{lambda^2/2}, so E max Z_n <= ln N / lambda + lambda/2 for every lambda > 0; lambda = sqrt(2 ln N) gives sqrt(2 ln N). The statement matches Lesson 1, Theorem 2.1 (L01.html line 82), whose scope is 'any joint distribution', and the L08 claim uses no wider scope. The index is the page's N (configurations), and the claim uses the N-1 nulls, with sqrt(2 ln(N-1)) <= sqrt(2 ln N). Concept link to L01 def-expected-maximum-sharpe exists (check_dag PASS). Card S7-c227 now covers it (L08-sec5-expected-max-card-gap).

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L08.html section 5, T span 'So as N grows, the null configurations win the in-sample contest at least as often' (line 272)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: New span checked. The genuine configuration's win probability P(Z + delta > Q_(N-1)) cannot rise with N (containment, L08-math-sec5-dilution), so the probability that some null configuration beats it, the complement, cannot fall: the statement is T and proved on the page. Numerical check (out_l08_sec5_monotone.txt): the win probability with k = 1..39 nulls is non-increasing. Card coverage: S7-c212 answers 'Can adding a null trial raise the probability that a genuine configuration wins in sample?' with 'No'; applied one null at a time, that is this span, so the span is covered by the card (accepted).

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L07.html Remark 2.9 (line 204): T span 'If SR = 0 and the variance is finite, sqrt(T) SR-hat = (sqrt(T) mu-hat/sigma)(sigma/sigma-hat) -> N(0,1), by the CLT for mu-hat, the LLN for sigma-hat and Slutsky's lemma'
rows.evidence: unchanged since 36e745a (git diff checked); round-16 evidence: Derivation re-checked step by step. (i) SR-hat = mu-hat/sigma-hat, so sqrt(T) SR-hat = (sqrt(T) mu-hat/sigma)(sigma/sigma-hat) is an identity. (ii) With iid returns, mean mu = SR sigma = 0 and finite variance sigma^2, the CLT gives sqrt(T) mu-hat/sigma -> N(0,1). (iii) sigma-hat^2 = (1/(T-1)) sum (r - r-bar)^2 -> sigma^2 in probability by the LLN applied to r^2 (finite since E r^2 < infinity) and r-bar -> 0; so sigma/sigma-hat -> 1 in probability (the divisor T or T-1 does not matter). (iv) Slutsky gives the limit N(0,1). Nothing beyond finite variance is used. Numerical spot check (scratch num_checks.py, 20000 replications): Student t with 3 df scaled to unit variance, SR = 0: P(z <= -1.6449) = 0.0513 / 0.0502 / 0.0502 and P(z <= 1.6449) = 0.9505 / 0.9500 / 0.9506 at T = 250 / 1000 / 4000 (N(0,1): 0.05 and 0.95); sd(z) = 1.007 / 1.001 / 0.992. The fourth moment is infinite there, so the check is of the claim's sufficiency. Grade T is right (proved on the page). The iid standing assumption is the section 1 assumption ('keep independence').

Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1214/aop/1024404523, fetched) title 'When is the Student $t$-statistic asymptotically standard normal?', authors Evarist Gine, Friedrich Götze, David M. Mason, pages 1514-1531, print 1997-07-01. Crossref abstract (verbatim, saved /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify32h-L07-L08/cr/crossref_abstracts.json): 'Let X, X_i, i in N, be independent, identically distributed random variables.
